Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
27-year-old woman with acute unilateral throbbing headache, visual aura, photophobia, and nausea/vomiting—clinically consistent with migraine.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Severe left-sided throbbing headache began around midday today; worsens with head/neck movement.  
• Associated symptoms: Preceded by “zig-zag” visual aura and transient blurred vision in both eyes; photophobia (wearing sunglasses); nausea with two episodes of vomiting; no fever, rash, speech difficulty, limb weakness, or balance problems.  
• Similar episode a few weeks ago lasting ~2 days, improved with rest and analgesics.  
• Past medical history: None reported.  
• Medications: 
  – Microgynon oral contraceptive, on for 3 months (dose not documented).  
• Allergies: Not discussed.  
• Family history: Mother with migraines and hypothyroidism; no known brain tumors in family.  
• Social/occupational: Works in fashion industry; high job stress; lives alone; non-smoker; does not drink alcohol; no regular exercise.  

Examination:
(No in-clinic examination findings documented.)  
Vitals: Not documented.  

Impression:
Likely migraine with aura. Serious intracranial pathology considered unlikely given current history.

Plan:
• Symptomatic treatment:  
  – Paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
  – Consider stronger analgesia such as Co-codamol (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
  – Non-steroidal anti-inflammatories: Ibuprofen or Naproxen (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
• Headache diary to identify frequency and potential triggers.  
• Discuss prophylactic migraine therapy if headaches become more frequent/persistent; review at next appointment (planned for next week).  
• Red-flag advice: Return immediately if headache worsens or fails to improve in 2–3 days, new neurological deficits (weakness, vision changes, speech problems), escalating neck pain, or other concerning symptoms.  
• Stress management and lifestyle modifications briefly encouraged; no specific plan documented.  

Quality checks:

● Missing expected elements: Allergies, detailed medications list with doses, vital signs, physical examination findings, documentation of over-the-counter vs prescription status, formal neurological exam.  
● Conflicts noted: None.  
● Transcript quality: Clear; minor conversational tangents but overall adequate for documentation.
